# Migrating from Persona

<!-- Generated by `pnpm --filter @openverify/docs-tools docs:catalog` (packages/docs-tools/src/catalog/); do not edit by hand. -->

OpenVerify is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by the vendor whose public API this page maps, or any other identity-verification vendor.

This page maps the public identifiers of a hosted identity-verification API (the "source API") to OpenVerify's, from the identifier index `docs/research/persona-surface.md` (the source's OpenAPI repository at version `2026-09-29` and its public pages, identifiers only) and OpenVerify's [OpenAPI document](../api/openapi.json). A row says where behaviour corresponds, or why it does not; it never claims that results are equivalent (C280.7). Identifiers are quoted as behaviour; no text of the source is copied.

The vendor-naming switch is on (Q8 granted): source identifiers are written as they are.

## Concerns

| Concern | Source API | OpenVerify | Migration note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base path | the source vendor's host, under `/api/v1` | `/api/v1/` on the operator's own host | Change the host; most path families keep their names (the tables below). |
| Authentication | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` | `Authorization: Bearer` with an API key (`ov_sbx_…` or `ov_prod_…`), scoped, with an optional address allowlist and expiry ([API keys](../settings/api-keys.md)) | Issue new keys; map each integration to the scopes it needs ([the API reference](../api/README.md)). |
| Version header | the source API's version header, dated values | `OpenVerify-Version`, dated values (C12) | Pin a version explicitly on both sides. |
| Key casing | a request header chooses camel, kebab or snake casing | kebab-case attributes only | A client that relies on camel or snake casing needs a mapping layer. |
| Idempotency | `Idempotency-Key` header | `Idempotency-Key`, answers kept 24 hours (C12) | The same header; the API reference says which operations take it. |
| Pagination | `page[after]`, `page[before]`, `page[size]` | `page[after]`, `page[size]`, and `page[before]` on one list only (`GET /api/v1/inquiries` has none) | Backward paging needs a change. |
| Webhook signature | the source API's signature header: `t=<unix>,v1=<hmac>` | `OpenVerify-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">`, one `v1` per active secret during rotation | The same scheme under another header name and secret; `@openverify/node` verifies it. |
| Ids | `<prefix>_` followed by a random string | `<prefix>_<ULID>` (`inq`, `itmpl`, `acc`, `ver`, `rep`, …) | Source ids cannot become OpenVerify ids: carry them in `reference-id` or an account field and keep a mapping table. |
| Checks and reports | names in example payloads | the [check catalog](../checks/catalog.md) | The tables below map each name; a result is never migrated as a passed check. |
| Events | resource events, `report/<type>.<action>` for reports | `EVENT_NAMES` (`@openverify/contracts`), the Connect events of C239 among them | Re-subscribe each webhook by name ([the API reference](../api/README.md#webhook-events)). |

## What does not migrate

- Historical captures and results are imported, if at all, as account fields or attachments labelled with their source, never as passed checks: they were not produced by OpenVerify's checks (rule 5, ADR 0002).
- A cloned-result route does not exist between platforms: Connect shares verifications between two organisations of one OpenVerify install only ([limits of sharing](../connect/limits.md)).
- Source ids do not carry over; keep them in `reference-id` or an account field with a mapping table.

Reason codes (C280.1): `next-release`, planned for the next release; `not-planned`, not in OpenVerify's plan; `licensed-data`, needs a licensed data source or an operator contract (OpenVerify ships adapters plus a deterministic sandbox provider for those it builds, rule 5); `vendor-retiring`, the source is retiring it.

## Signal, session, device and network identifiers (Phase 7)

From the identifier index, as it records them: Added 2026-10-30 (Workflow 7A Stage 1a, plan C109) from `docs/research/phase7-behaviour.md`, which read the public documentation pages these come from; the OpenAPI repository this index was extracted from holds none of them. Identifiers only; how each maps to OpenVerify is in `docs/plans/phase-7.plan.md` C90, C91 and C110.

| Item | Identifiers, and how OpenVerify serves them where the index says |
|---|---|
| Resources | `device` (path `devices`, above) and `network` (no path: reached only as an inquiry session's relationship and through `include`). |
| Inquiry session attributes | `os-name`, `os-full-version`, `browser-name`, `browser-full-version`, `device-type`, `device-name`, `mobile-sdk-name`, `mobile-sdk-full-version`, `device-handoff-method`, `is-tor`, `is-datacenter`, `is-vpn`, `is-proxy`, `threat-level`, `country-code`, `country-name`, `region-code`, `region-name`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `gps-latitude`, `gps-longitude`, `gps-precision`, `gps-country-code`, `ip-connection-type`, `ip-isp`, `network-organization`. |
| Device attributes | `device-vendor-id`, `device-fingerprint`, `browser-fingerprint`. |
| Network attributes | `ip-address`, `service-provider`, `service-type`, `proxy-type`, `threat-level` (with `unknown`), `country-code`, `country-name`, `region-code`, `region-name`, `latitude`, `longitude`. |
| Inquiry attributes | `signals` (an array of `{ name, value }`, documented outside the OpenAPI inquiry schema) and `behaviors` (in the OpenAPI inquiry schema; its meaning is not documented, deferred in C110). |
| Inquiry signal names | `inquiry/bot_score`, `inquiry/behavior_threat_level`, `inquiry/country_from_session`, `inquiry/country_comparison`, `inquiry/geolocation_to_residency_delta`, `inquiry/last_two_verifications_geolocation_delta`. |
| Events | `session.created` and `session.expired` appear on the events page; their meaning beside `inquiry-session.*` is not documented, so they are not registered (C110). |
| Report type `ip-address` (above) with its public result attributes `service-type`, `datacenter-ip`, `vpn-detected`, `proxy-detected`, `tor-exit-node`, `isp`, `mobile-ip`, `country-code`, `country-name`, `city`, `region`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `error`. | - |

## Android SDK identifiers (Phase 10)

From the identifier index, as it records them: Added 2026-11-09 (Workflow 10A Stage 4, plan C222) from `docs/research/phase10-android-behaviour.md` (gap rows M3 to M11, M32, M38), which read the public documentation pages these come from. Identifiers only, each marked **built**, **kept** (today's behaviour, documented) or **not built**; how each maps to OpenVerify is in `docs/plans/phase-10.plan.md` C190 to C192 and `docs/android/`.

| Item | Identifiers, and how OpenVerify serves them where the index says |
|---|---|
| Entry points | `fromInquiry` with `sessionToken`: kept, as `OpenVerifyInquiry.Request(inquiryId, sessionToken, apiBaseUrl)` with the token always required. `fromOneTimeLinkCode`: kept, as `fromOneTimeLink(url, apiBaseUrl)` and `OneTimeLinkContract`, the API always the host's (C190.2). `fromTemplate`, `fromTemplateVersion`: not built (inquiries are created by the customer's server; C223). `toInlineInquiryBuilder`, `createFragment`, `InlineInquiryScreen`: not built (inline mode deferred; C223). |
| Builder options | `locale`: built (`Request.locale`, C190.2, C199.2). `styleVariant` (`LIGHT`, `DARK`): built as `appearance` (`SYSTEM`, `LIGHT`, `DARK`; C198.5). `environment`, `environmentId`, `referenceId`, `accountId`, `fields`: not built on the client, set when the server creates the inquiry (C190.1). `shareToken`, `fieldMappings`: not built (Phase 11 Connect). |
| Result outcomes | `Complete` (`inquiryId`, `status`): kept as `InquiryResult.Completed(inquiryId, inquiryStatus)`, with no `fields`. `Cancel` (`inquiryId`): kept as `Canceled(inquiryId)`, with no `sessionToken`. `Error` (`debugMessage`, `errorCode`): built as `Failed(inquiryId, reason)` over a closed, published `FailureReason` list with `FLOW_HALTED` added (C190.4, `docs/android/failure-reasons.md`). |
| Events | `onEventListener`: built as `OpenVerifyComponents.eventListener` (C192). `StartEvent`: built as `OpenVerifyEvent.Started`. `MiscInquiryEvent` (step transition, camera permission, camera failure, upload): built as `StepShown`, `CameraPermission`, `CaptureFailed`, `Submitted`, `Waiting` and `Ended`, PII-free by an allowlist test (`docs/android/events.md`). |
| Resource-name overrides (images, animations, the loader's style) | not built (C223). |
| Optional modules (Workflow 10E, 2026-11-11) | an NFC module that reads a document's chip: built as `openverify-nfc` (`OpenVerifyNfc.chipReader`, on JMRTD; proved on the build host against a synthetic chip, no real document read yet; `docs/android/nfc.md`). On-device face detection for selfie guidance: built as `openverify-face` (`OpenVerifyFace.detectorFactory`, YuNet through ONNX Runtime; guidance only, never a liveness verdict; `docs/android/capture.md`). A device-attestation client: not built (the owner declined a Google Play Integrity artifact; a host implements `IntegrityTokenProvider` itself, `docs/android/device-integrity.md`). Publication to a public Maven repository: not done (pending the owner's accounts; the staged local repository is the release). |

## Connect: scopes and entry points (C280.1)

| Source | OpenVerify | Note |
|---|---|---|
| scope `connect.read` | `connect-connections:read`, `connect-share-tokens:read` | renamed (connect R19) |
| scope `connect.write` | `connect-connections:write`, `connect-share-tokens:write` | renamed; redeeming is `connect-share-tokens:redeem` and peeking `connect-share-tokens:peek` (ours, narrower) |
| scope `connect_connection.read` | `connect-connections:read` | renamed |
| scope `connect_connection.write` | `connect-connections:write` | renamed; activation is the console's, with a second factor (C231.3) |
| scope `connect_share_token.read` | `connect-share-tokens:read`; `peek-source-data` needs `connect-share-tokens:peek` | renamed |
| scope `connect_share_token.write` | `connect-share-tokens:write`; redeeming needs `connect-share-tokens:redeem` | renamed |
| the mobile SDK option `shareToken` (and `fieldMappings`) | not on the client: the customer's server creates the inquiry with `meta.share-token-id`, and the SDK renders the `share_consent` step it is given | no token reaches the client (C238.5, C238.7) |
| the hosted flow entry with `inquiry-id` and `share-token` | `meta.share-token-id` on the inquiry create, then the flow's `share-consent` step | no token in any URL (C238.5; review H24) |
